To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a significant difference in the textural features of MRI volumes of healthy and AD subjects; (2) the differences in textural features can be used to distinguish AD from healthy subjects; (3) the textural differences are not only due to atrophy of the hippocampus but to other parts of the brain as well.
the textural information in the brain is sufficient to distinguish between healthy and diseased tissue, and that the information is sufficient to identify the type of malformation in diseased tissue.
we have a new method of textural analysis of 3D MRI images that is able to identify the earliest structural malformations of AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for textural analysis of MR images.
the development and evaluation of a method for texturally characterising 3D MRI images.
developing a method of analysis of the 3D textures of MRI images of the brain, which is able to identify the early stages of AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research has produced a novel approach to the problem of textural description in 3D, which has the potential for use in the diagnosis of brain malformations due to Alzheimer's disease.
the method we describe is a new approach to the classification and assessment of AD.
the textural 3D analysis is a powerful tool for the detection of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method of textural analysis for MRI volumes of the human brain, based upon a wavelet representation of the texture.

we have developed a new method for the analysis of the textural features in the brain and that we have demonstrated that this method is useful in detecting and identifying the earliest structural changes in the brain due to AD.
we have developed a new model for textural description, based upon a 3D wavelet transform, which allows us to characterise the textural properties of MRI brain scans, in a unique way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to be useful in the diagnosis of AD, a method of textural feature extraction must be robust, unambiguous, and reliable.
, by applying our method to a database of MR images of patients, we are able to detect and identify AD with an accuracy of 95% (using the 3D textural features).

, using a combination of 3D textural analysis and symbolic descriptions, we have been able to construct a reliable database of information about the structure and texture of the brain in MRI images, which we believe is a significant advance in our understanding of the textural structure of the brain and the early detection of AD.
